correctness.rationale: For any rank-q error, direct thin-SVD algebra yields active signed coefficients s_i-t*sum(s). The exact quadratic line search has t=1/q. This produces equality of the two absolute residual singular values after one step for all rank-two errors, and a second zero step. At every rank >=3, the positive spectrum proportional to (1,...,1,r-1) reproduces itself with nonzero factor (r-2)/r indefinitely. Equal starting singular values force t=1/r for any fixed step claimed to terminate universally; the higher-rank ray obstructs it. The exact-line-search first-step rank discontinuity squared norm is 8/3. Standalone rational/matrix checker verify.py passed 7401 finite checks, corroborating but not replacing the proof in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The step is exactly the optimal line search for a natural spectral-norm steepest-descent method, rather than a tuned artificial recurrence. The classification exhausts which matrix ranks admit uniform finite termination on an isotropic strongly convex quadratic. The sharp rank-two versus rank-three dichotomy, explicit nonterminating geometric ray, and quantified rank-raising discontinuity distinguish finite-step reliability from known linear-rate estimates and expose a practically relevant fragility of exact polar algorithms.
